q1.prompt: The SALES_BY_STORE view is built from which base tables? (Read the text column in the SHOW VIEWS output above.)

a.feedback: Correct! The view selects FROM STORES and LEFT JOINs ORDERS on store_id.

b.feedback: Not quite — re-read the FROM / JOIN in the view's text.

c.feedback: Close, but CUSTOMERS isn't referenced — check the view's text.

d.feedback: A view can read more than one table — look for the JOIN in its text.

q2.prompt: Your query context in Snowflake is made up of which four things?

a.feedback: Correct! Context = role · warehouse · database · schema. Setting it makes your results predictable.

b.feedback: Those identify your session/account — the query context is role, warehouse, database, and schema.

c.feedback: Those are object levels, not your session context (role, warehouse, database, schema).

d.text: Warehouse size, credits, role, and user
d.feedback: Not quite — context is role, warehouse, database, and schema.

q3.prompt: What is the correct top-to-bottom object hierarchy in Snowflake?

a.feedback: Correct! Objects nest account → database → schema → table/view.

b.feedback: The account is the top level, above databases.

c.feedback: Reversed — it's account → database → schema → table/view.

d.feedback: Databases contain schemas, not the other way around.

q4.prompt: In this course, where do you create and own the objects you build?

a.text: In your own database (e.g. USER_DB); the shared PLATPLUS_DB is read-only to you
a.feedback: Correct! You build in your own database; PLATPLUS_DB is shared and read-only, so you can't break it.

b.feedback: PLATPLUS_DB is shared and read-only — you create in your own database instead.

c.feedback: That's a system database you only read from. You build in your own database.

d.feedback: You can — in your own database, which you own.

q5.prompt: You discover that FEEDBACK.comment contains free-text customer reviews. What should you do before granting SELECT on FEEDBACK to a new analyst role?

a.text: Run SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE FEEDBACK to see who already has access
a.feedback: Correct! You need the current state before you change it. SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE tells you every role with any privilege on that object — your governance baseline before Lab 3.

b.text: Run SELECT * FROM FEEDBACK to check the data is safe
b.feedback: Reading the data doesn't tell you who else can read it. SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE shows the access picture without requiring you to inspect the content.

c.text: Grant SELECT immediately — you can always revoke it later
c.feedback: Grant-then-revoke is a compliance risk. The right order is: understand current access → design the intended state → grant or revoke to match.

d.text: Ask the DBA who originally loaded the data
d.feedback: SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE gives you the authoritative answer in seconds — faster and more reliable than a conversation.
